PullRequest.Title: Add PR comment on selection in Agents

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event registration, synchronous call chain, linear loop, and before/after placement are explicit in the repository. The only material uncertainty is how often users have very large session change sets, so severity is medium rather than high; the experiment can be auto-enabled despite its false default.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous CPU work scanning session change entries and allocating replacement menu actions
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is O(selection events × session changes), plus O(selection events × associated pull requests); keyboard range extension generates one cursor-selection event per key repeat.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased editor input latency and selection jank for sessions with large change sets when the PR-comments experiment is enabled.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary non-empty cursor selections opened/repositioned the feedback widget without resolving PR comment context. The change-list scan occurred only when the user explicitly invoked the line/gutter comment flow.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every qualifying cursor-selection event now calls getPRReviewCommentPullRequests synchronously before showing the widget. For normal file resources that call enters _getPRReviewCommentContext and _resolveWorkspaceResource, which walks session.changes and compares up to three URIs per change; the result is then used to rebuild disposable Action objects.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added argument `this._getPRCommentPullRequests(sessionResource, model.uri)` at RIGHT line 427 is executed from `_onSelectionChanged`, which is directly registered to `onDidChangeCursorSelection`. Before this hunk `_show` was called with only geometry/focus arguments, so selections did not enter the PR-context/change-list scan.
Findings.Title: Cache PR context off the cursor-selection path
Findings.Impact: With `chat.experimental.agentsWindowPRComments` enabled, extending a selection via the keyboard in a session containing hundreds or thousands of changed files repeatedly scans that entire list on the editor event path, delaying each selection update and causing visible input lag. A file absent from or late in the list exercises the full scan.
Findings.Evidence: `_onSelectionChanged` is called by `editor.onDidChangeCursorSelection` (line 213). The new call reaches `CodeReviewService.getPRReviewCommentPullRequests` -> `_getPRReviewCommentContext` (codeReviewService.ts:308-329) -> `_resolveWorkspaceResource` (403-411), whose `for (const change of changes ?? [])` compares each change's URI candidates until a match is found. `_show` then calls `_setInputPRCommentActions`, and `FeedbackInputWidget.setAdditionalActions` clears and recreates actions. Mouse dragging is coalesced by `_mouseDown`, but Shift+Arrow/keyboard selection changes are not, so repeated key events synchronously repeat the full scan before widget positioning.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve and cache the PR context/actions once per session and model resource, invalidating it when the session change list, workspace GitHub metadata, model, or setting changes; alternatively defer the lookup until the split-button menu is opened. Keep cursor-selection handling limited to range/position updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select or extend a code range while the feedback widget is available and PR comments are enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `onDidChangeCursorSelection` synchronously runs `_onSelectionChanged`, resolves the feedback session, resolves PR context, rebuilds additional actions, shows/repositions the widget, and only then returns control to the editor. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation occurs on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Keyboard selection event count multiplied by the active session's cumulative changed-file count; associated PR count additionally controls transient menu-action allocation. Mouse-drag changes are suppressed until mouseup, but Shift+Arrow/key-repeat changes are not.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous on the editor/UI event path; no batching, debounce, or coalescing for keyboard selection events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session lookup itself has active/last-session caching, but the newly reached PR-context path has no per-resource cache and rescans `session.changes` on every event. PR action instances are cleared and recreated on every qualifying selection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added argument is directly in the cursor-selection handler, and the transitive `for` loop over `session.changes` is synchronous and uncached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact delay depends on experiment rollout and session change-set size. Hundreds or thousands of changes are less common, which bounds severity, but the multiplicative mechanism is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity selection latency regression; finding submitted at the newly added call.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose “Add PR Comment” for a selected range and resolve its GitHub target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the explicit action, target resolution refreshes the selected PR, fetches changed files, fetches head file content, computes a full-file line diff, parses the patch, and validates the selected range. All remote reads and local diff work must finish before posting can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh pull request details and reviews with two concurrent conditional REST requests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two requests for the one explicitly selected PR; concurrent within `Promise.all` and coalesced only with an already in-flight refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing gutter/line PR-comment workflow performed the same model refresh before opening its input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both requests must complete before target resolution can read head SHA and pending review state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch all changed-file pages for the selected pull request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per 100 changed files, serially paginated, for one selected PR; no service-level cache is visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing gutter/line PR-comment workflow performed this fetch during target resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before locating the selected file's patch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and base64-decode the selected file at the PR head SHA
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One REST request for the one selected PR/file; no cache is visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing gutter/line PR-comment workflow fetched the same head content during target resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before current-to-PR range mapping.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one selected PR after dropdown choice; changed-file pagination scales by ceil(PR files/100), while local diff CPU/allocation scales with head/current file line counts and patch validation scales with changed/selected lines.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two PR refresh requests run concurrently; changed-file pages are serial; file content follows changed files; local diff follows file content. Separate user submissions are guarded by widget busy state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR refresh uses ETags and coalesces overlapping refreshes, but still performs conditional requests. Changed-file and file-content reads are uncached. Failures are not negative-cached. Passing a selected PR prevents multi-PR fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub latency and PR/file size vary, but all boundaries and ordering are explicit. They occur only after an explicit PR-comment action and are not added to ordinary selection by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new selection-based feature reaches expensive target resolution only after explicit submission, and equivalent PR-comment creation already required this sequence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Post a single-line or multi-line PR review comment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected target is posted through either GraphQL for an existing pending review or REST for a new review, then review threads are force-refreshed before the widget is dismissed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post one review thread/comment using GraphQL or REST
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request for the chosen PR and comment; `startLine`/`startSide` only add constant-size fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Single-line PR comments already made one corresponding post request; the diff changes payload shape to support a range.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GraphQL refresh for the chosen PR after the post.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same forced refresh already followed PR-comment posting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the add operation completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One comment and one chosen PR. Payload grows only by two scalar range fields. Range validation is linear in selected lines but successful validation is bounded by the already materialized set of commentable patch lines.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Post and refresh are deliberately serialized. Widget busy state prevents duplicate concurrent submissions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Posting is intentionally uncached. Review-thread refresh bypasses stale state with the existing force-refresh behavior; no new retained cache keys are introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network duration varies, but request cardinality is fixed and unchanged for equivalent posting.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: multi-line support does not add request fan-out or meaningful serialization/allocation growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Poll and render unresolved GitHub review threads, including multi-line threads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each associated PR, existing polling fetches review threads; observable recomputation maps each unresolved thread to one comment range consumed by editor/change-view surfaces.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch review threads through the existing GraphQL query
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GraphQL call per associated PR per existing refresh/poll cycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same query and per-PR polling existed; the diff requests one additional scalar `startLine` field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial review state waits for each model's first refresh; later polling is background work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Associated PR count and unresolved thread count; each thread still maps to one Range object regardless of its line span.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing service autoruns establish one model/poller per associated PR; this diff does not change their scheduling or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing referenced review-thread models and polling lifecycle are unchanged. Adding `startLine` does not add cache entries or alter invalidation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Thread and PR counts vary, but added response size is one nullable integer per thread and no new work scales with the number of lines in a range during mapping.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: constant metadata growth and a wider range value do not establish a rendering or memory regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one finding for an uncached O(selection events × session changes) scan newly placed on the editor selection path. Traced PR-target lookup, posting, refresh/polling, range mapping, cache behavior, and request concurrency; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.
